title: Glitch halts inquest; Probe into death of 2 men at police station delayed until broadcast feed restored
article: The second day of a coroner's inquest into the deaths of Jamie Goodwin and Ricardo Wesley was delayed for more than two hours yesterday while a technical glitch was ironed out and a live broadcast feed of the proceedings could be restored to the men's hometown.
Goodwin, 20, and Wesley, 22, were trapped in their cells on Jan. 8, 2006, as the Kashechewan police station where they were being held burned to the ground, killing them both.

The inquest proceedings were shifted to Toronto, but the coroner's office had promised to establish a link with a school room in the isolated First Nations community of Kashechewan so that people there could watch. However, the link didn't work Monday.
"The fire was tragic and affected many of our people," Kasechewan Chief Johnathan Solomon said. "Seeing the inquest unfold is extremely important to my people as it will assist in their healing."
The people in Kashechewan, including Wesley's mom, Eileen, are frustrated at the delays, he said.
Eileen Wesley said in a statement issued by the Nishnawbe Aski Nation that she was disappointed not to be able to watch the inquest as it started.
"I feel extremely anxious, let down and left out of this whole process. I'm unhappy not knowing what was said about my son," she said.

But the presiding coroner, Dr. David Eden, promised to rectify the situation and apologized for the technical glitches and wouldn't start yesterday's testimony from OPP Supt. Brad Blair until the problem could be fixed.
He has promised to make a recording of Monday's proceedings available to anyone in Kashechewan who wants to view it.
The testimony yesterday was designed to provide the three-man, two-woman coroner's jury with some context about the structure of policing in Ontario's north.
